current_assessment: The science spectrometer detector array has failed and is unresponsive to restart commands. The instrument has been placed in safe mode. Camera and radiation sensor remain operational. The primary science instrument for this Europa flyby phase is unavailable. This is a significant mission impact but not a spacecraft safety concern.

predicted_failures.failure_mode: Camera detector degradation from unshielded radiation exposure (spectrometer normally provides shielding)
early_warning_signs: Camera dark frame noise floor increase
Hot pixel count above 0.1% of array

predicted_failures.failure_mode: Spectrometer power regulator fault spreading to instrument power bus

cascading_risks: Primary science objective for Europa flyby is unachievable without spectrometer
Spectrometer power regulator fault may indicate wider instrument bus issue
Safe mode power cycling may have corrupted science data buffer — data recovery uncertain
recommended_actions: Attempt cold restart after 4-hour thermal stabilisation period
Redirect camera to capture contextual imaging of spectrometer target regions as partial mitigation
Increase radiation sensor sampling rate to 10Hz to partially compensate for lost spectral data
Preserve all spectrometer memory dumps for ground analysis of failure mode
Assess whether remaining flyby objectives can be partially achieved with camera and radiation data alone

SCIENCE REPORT — ASTERIA-7 T+09:42

FDIR EVENT: Spectrometer detector array failure. Instrument unresponsive. Placed in safe mode.

CURRENT STATUS: Primary science instrument OFFLINE. Spacecraft health nominal. Camera and radiation sensor operational.

PRIMARY RISK: Europa flyby primary science objective unachievable in current configuration. Cold restart to be attempted after 4-hour cooldown.

ACTIONS TAKEN BY FDIR: Power cycle attempted, buffers flushed, instrument safe mode activated.

GROUND RECOMMENDATIONS: (1) Authorise cold restart attempt at T+4h. (2) Approve revised flyby science plan using camera + radiation sensor. (3) Request failure mode analysis from instrument team.

MISSION IMPACT: Primary science collection lost for this flyby. Spacecraft safe. Recovery possible.
